display.purpose: Hero headlines on landing, registration, OTP, empty-feed first-visit. Never inside the app shell.

headline.purpose: Page titles inside the shell. Section anchors like 'People you may know'.

title.purpose: Post author names, profile names, nav-item labels at the larger end.

body.purpose: Post content, comment content, long-form copy. Cap at 65–75ch.

meta.purpose: Captions, department/batch strings, timestamps, helper text under inputs.

label.purpose: Eyebrows ('campus tools', 'trending now') and badge text. Letter-spaced, not uppercased.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: The only permitted box-shadow. Used on :focus-visible for keyboard navigation indicators.

shadows.name: input-focus
shadows.purpose: Wider, soft focus ring on text inputs, paired with a border shift to --uc-indigo.

motion.name: ease-out-strong
motion.purpose: Default exponential ease-out. Used on dropdown entrances, press feedback, progress bar fills.

motion.name: ease-in-out-strong
motion.purpose: Symmetric ease for back-and-forth state shifts (modal open/close).

motion.name: duration-slow
motion.purpose: Progress bar fills, poll bar reveals.

breakpoints.name: mobile
breakpoints.purpose: Below this width, sidebars hide and the mobile bottom nav + More sheet take over.

breakpoints.name: tablet-right
breakpoints.purpose: Below this width, the right rail hides. Left rail stays visible.

breakpoints.name: desktop
breakpoints.purpose: Max-width cap on the feed grid; content centers.

narrative.overview:
UniConnecT is the campus after last bell. The quads are dim, the residence halls glow in their windows, and the people still moving — students between assignments, alumni catching up, faculty pinning tomorrow's notice — move with intention. The UI is the building that holds them. Dark navy surfaces are the walls. UIU orange is the institutional lamp that marks you: your post, your bookmark, your milestone. UC indigo is the network around you: the rooms you visit, the peers you find. The job of every screen is to recede so the people and the work surface; nothing in the chrome should clamor for attention.

This system explicitly rejects the consumer-social aesthetic (Facebook with a UIU logo), the SaaS-template look (Notion beige + indigo brand), and the engagement-bait gravity (algorithmic suggestion noise, infinite-scroll dark patterns, bright red 'you have unread' dots screaming for taps). It also rejects the first-order AI reflexes for the social-product category: glassmorphism, gradient hero copy, identical icon-and-heading card grids, glow effects under buttons. Warmth comes from context-awareness and good defaults, not decoration.

Density is product-density: information-dense at small sizes, mobile-first, designed to survive mid-tier Android on slow campus 4G. Hairline 0.5px borders carry structure; pill radii (999px) carry interaction; sentence case carries voice. The system has two interactive accents (orange and indigo) with strictly assigned roles, six surface tints, one body face (Inter), one display face (Fraunces). Variety happens through hierarchy and rhythm, never through new shapes.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-surface only. Surface stacking, never shadows, for depth.
Two-accent palette. Orange = self; indigo = peer/system. The roles are not interchangeable.
0.5px hairlines everywhere. 1px borders are reserved for badge counters and avatar gaps.
Pill (999px) for every button. Card radius is 16px. No sharp corners.
Sentence case. Always. No ALL CAPS, no Title Case On Buttons.
Weight 400 / 500 only. 600+ does not exist in this system.
Mobile is not 'responsive desktop'. Layout collapses meaningfully (sidebars → bottom nav with a More sheet), not by hiding columns.

rules.name: The Self / Network Rule
rules.body: Orange marks the user themselves (their identity, their content, their actions). Indigo marks the system and their peers. The two accents are not interchangeable. If you're about to put indigo on a 'you saved this' affordance, or orange on a 'peer suggestion', stop and pick again.

rules.name: The 28%-Alpha Floor
rules.body: Any text the user is expected to read must use --text-primary or --text-secondary. The 28%-alpha --text-tertiary is for scannable metadata only (timestamps, eyebrows, 'Done' labels), never for explanatory copy.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Structural borders are 0.5px, color --border-default. The only exceptions are the 1.5px avatar-cover gap, the 1.5px UIU-orange avatar ring on the profile mini-card, and the 1.5px white border around mobile-nav badge dots.

rules.name: The Sentence-Case Rule
rules.body: All UI labels — buttons, nav items, badges, section headers — are sentence case. The only place capital-letter prominence comes from is the letter-spaced label tier, and even there the visible characters stay lowercase.

rules.name: The Two-Weight Rule
rules.body: This system has exactly two weights: regular (400) for body copy and meta, medium (500) for titles, labels, and emphasis. Weights 600 / 700 / 800 do not exist. If you reach for one, increase the size instead.

rules.name: The Hierarchy-Through-Scale Rule
rules.body: The scale ratio between adjacent steps is ≥1.25. Flat scales (13px → 14px → 15px → 16px) read as decoration; the ratio is what makes hierarchy legible without color.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: This system has no box-shadow for depth. Surfaces stack through a four-tier tint progression. The only box-shadow permitted in the system is the 2px ring used on :focus-visible.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: box-shadow is reserved for :focus-visible rings. If you need depth, climb the surface stack. If you need hover feedback, change the border to --border-hover or the background to --surface-hover.

rules.name: The Ghost-Border Fallback
rules.body: Where a 0.5px border at --border-default is too quiet, step the border to --border-hover before reaching for anything stronger. Background lift is the next step; new colors are the step after that.

dos: Do use UIU Cinder Orange (#F05A28) for things that are yours — your active filter, your saved bookmark, your progress, your avatar ring.
Do use Campus Twilight Indigo (#5B5BD6) for the network around you — peer suggestions, primary CTAs, nav active states, event date boxes, trending tags.
Do keep every border 0.5px solid var(--border-default) unless there's a specific reason to step up. 1px is loud in this system.
Do climb the surface stack for depth: --surface-page → --surface-card → --surface-raised → --surface-hover. Tint, not shadow.
Do use pill (999px) radii on every button and every chip. Card radius is 16px (--r-lg).
Do write all UI labels in sentence case. 'Save' not 'SAVE', 'People you may know' not 'People You May Know'.
Do use weight 400 for body and 500 for emphasis. There are no other weights.
Do keep --text-tertiary (28% alpha) for scannable metadata only — timestamps, eyebrows, faint counters.
Do design mobile-first behavior, not 'responsive desktop'. Sidebars collapse to a real More sheet that exposes every route.
Do render skeletons that preserve final layout (sized boxes shaped like the data they'll be replaced by).
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion — global rule in index.css already disables animation/transition duration.
donts: Don't look like consumer social (Facebook / Instagram). No engagement-bait patterns, no algorithmic suggestion noise, no blue-heavy identity.
Don't look like SaaS-template UI. No SaaS-cream light mode, no Notion-style beige, no 'productivity tool' indigo-with-glow look.
Don't use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe. The announcement banner uses a full-width tinted strip with a bottom border, never a side stripe.
Don't use background-clip: text with a gradient. No gradient headlines, no gradient buttons, no gradient anything.
Don't use glassmorphism. No backdrop-filter: blur(...) on cards, modals, or chrome.
Don't use box-shadow for depth. Focus rings only.
Don't nest cards. A card containing a card is always wrong here. Use 0.5px row dividers inside a card if you need sectioning.
Don't use Title Case or ALL CAPS on labels.
Don't use weights 600, 700, or 800. If a step needs more weight, increase the size instead.
Don't put gray text on a coloured background. Text on --uc-orange-bg uses --uc-orange-l. Text on --uc-indigo-bg uses --uc-indigo-l or --uc-indigo-xl.
Don't hide the scrollbar entirely (scrollbar-width: none). Use the .rail-scroll utility.
Don't ship a feature without empty / loading / error states matched to the filter or query context.

Don't use transition: width or transition: height for state changes. Width-fill on plain progress bars is the one exception; for fills that overlap content (poll bars), use a transform: scaleX() underlay with transform-origin: left center.
Don't introduce em dashes (—) into UI copy. Use a colon, a comma, a period, or parentheses.
